title: Identical rented units, numbered once

blocks.text: A storm-response team (not GridCap) rents identical mobile units for the season. Each outage site needs one unit for a number of days, a unit serves its sites one after another, and each unit is rented for 30 days. `build` in `fleet.py` already has the model: $`x_{s,k} = 1`$ if site $`s`$ is served by unit $`k`$, $`y_k = 1`$ if unit $`k`$ is rented, and
Renumbering the units gives the same plan, so every plan appears many times. Write `add_symmetry_breaking(fleet, days, units)`: rows that refuse every numbering that breaks one of these two rules:

items: the rented units are the first ones (no unit is rented while a lower-numbered one is not), and

the sites, taken in the order the dict `days` lists them (its key order, as given, not sorted by their number of days), fill the units in order: site number $`n`$ (from 0) may only use units $`0, \dots, n`$. `fleet.py`'s own 14 sites happen to be listed longest first; one test's sites are not.

blocks.text: Unlike the lesson's crews, here a unit can stay unrented, so decide what the first rule means as a row on the $`y`$. Before coding, write both families with their labels and argue on paper that every plan can be renumbered to satisfy both at once, so the fewest units cannot change. Check the second family on the first site: which units may it use?

Then run `fleet.py`: it solves the same 14 sites with and without your rows and prints HiGHS's node counts. Write down both. The lesson found that ordering rows can cost nodes as well as save them; see which happens here.
The tests fix whole plans and ask whether each is allowed, so any rows that keep this numbering pass. About six lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from datetime import timedelta

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from fleet import build

days = {"Ash": 18, "Elm": 15, "Oak": 11, "Yew": 10, "Fir": 6}

for ordered in (False, True):
    fleet = build(days, 4, ordered=ordered)
    result = mathopt.solve(fleet.model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS,
                           params=mathopt.SolveParameters(time_limit=timedelta(seconds=5)))
    print(f"ordered={ordered} rows:", sum(1 for _ in fleet.model.linear_constraints()))
    print(f"ordered={ordered} units rented:", round(result.objective_value()),
          {s: k for (s, k), v in fleet.x.items() if result.variable_values(v) > 0.5})

cases.says: with your rows the fewest units is unchanged, a plan numbered in order is allowed, and the same plan shifted to start at unit 1 is refused
a plan that rents unit 2 while unit 1 stays idle is refused
a plan that puts the first site on the second unit is refused
a plan numbered by first site whose unit 0 carries fewer days than unit 1 stays allowed
